task_name: MACE-MP-0 Foundation Model Reproduction and Validation
scientific_goal: Develop and validate a universal foundation model for atomistic simulations that covers the periodic table, stably simulates diverse material systems, and achieves quantitative accuracy with minimal fine-tuning

methodological_commitments.description: Higher-order equivariant message passing neural networks with body order > 2, using tensor product structure for efficient computation
Materials Project Trajectory Dataset with ~1.5 million inorganic crystal structures and relaxation trajectories
methodological_commitments.source: paper_001.pdf (Deng et al.), paper_003.pdf (Huang et al.)

methodological_commitments.description: Liquid water RDF, adsorption energy scaling relations on transition metal surfaces, CRBH20 reaction barriers

target_comparison_axes: Adsorption energy scaling relations (*O vs *OH) on fcc(111) transition metal surfaces
Reaction barrier heights for CRBH20 subset (Rxn 1, 11, 20)
expected_figure_families: Data overview: Element distribution in MPtrj dataset
Water RDF: g_OO(r), g_OH(r), g_HH(r) comparison
Scaling relations: E_ads(*O) vs E_ads(*OH) for Ni, Cu, Rh, Pd, Ir, Pt
Reaction barriers: MACE vs DFT comparison for CRBH20 reactions
Learning curves: Error vs training set size
Model architecture diagram: MACE message passing structure
interpretability_artifacts: Body order analysis: Effect of nu (correlation order) on accuracy
Equivariance analysis: Effect of L (symmetry order) on learning curves
Element-wise error distribution across periodic table
